posts.text:
Web3 Fundamentals (15 lessons): Wallets and Private Keys.
A wallet signs messages and transactions. In self-custody, you control keys or permissions; a custodian controls them for you. A signature proves account control, not legal identity.
posts.alt: Wallet control is not legal identity. A real public lesson excerpt and a separate authored lesson summary. Web3 Fundamentals · Lesson 5 of 15; Lesson summary · authored; A wallet signs messages and transactions. A signature proves account control, not legal identity. Screenshot text: In a self-custodial wallet, you control the keys or account permissions. Custodial services manage those controls on your behalf. A signature proves control of an account, not a person's legal identity.

posts.text:
Decentralized Finance (9 lessons): Lending and Borrowing in DeFi.
Example: 80% LTV on $1,000 collateral gives an $800 borrowing cap. Liquidation uses a separate threshold, with parameters set per market.
posts.alt: Borrowing cap and liquidation threshold differ. A real public lesson excerpt and a separate authored lesson summary. Decentralized Finance · Lesson 2 of 9 · Illustrative amounts; Lesson summary · authored; Example: 80% LTV on $1,000 collateral gives an $800 borrowing cap. Liquidation uses a separate threshold, with parameters set per market. Screenshot text: A collateralized position generally needs collateral worth more than the borrowed amount. The permitted loan-to-value ratio depends on the asset, market, and configured risk parameters.

posts.text:
Smart Contract Development (9 lessons): Testing Smart Contracts.
The sample transfers 100 units from a 1,000-unit balance and asserts 100 received, 900 left. Foundry fuzz tests then vary the amount to test properties.
posts.alt: Turn a transfer into explicit assertions. A real public lesson excerpt and a separate authored lesson summary. Foundry fuzz tests then vary the amount to test properties. Screenshot text: function test_Transfer() public {;   token.transfer(alice, 100);;   assertEq(token.balanceOf(alice), 100);

posts.text:
Web3 Marketing & Community (8 lessons): Growth Metrics and Analytics.
Unique Active Wallets counts addresses over a defined period. One person can control several. Retention asks how many wallets in a starting cohort return later.
posts.alt: Count wallets, then define the returning cohort. A real public lesson excerpt and a separate authored lesson summary. Web3 Marketing & Community · Lesson 5 of 8 · Measurement units; Lesson summary · authored; Unique Active Wallets counts addresses over a defined period. One person can control several. Retention asks how many wallets in a starting cohort return later. Screenshot text: Define what each dataset measures: accounts, addresses, transactions, sessions, or people. Avoid combining these as though they were the same unit.

posts.text:
AI x Crypto Intersection (7 lessons): Autonomous Agents.
Separate model, tools and wallet. Balance reads should not grant transfer-signing permission. Enforce spending caps and contract allowlists.
